column5: What is Claude Code and how does it differ from browser-based AI tools?
column6: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-native AI agent that runs in your shell with direct access to your filesystem, git history, and CLI tools. Unlike browser-based AI, it can read and edit your files, run commands, and interact with your infrastructure directly — no copy-pasting required.\n\nRemember: Claude Code = Anthropic's AI coding assistant CLI. Works in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps write, debug, and refactor code.

column5: What is CLAUDE.md and what is it used for?
column6: CLAUDE.md is a project context file that Claude Code reads automatically on startup. It contains project conventions, stack details, validation commands, and behavioral rules (like files not to modify). It supports a hierarchy: global (~/) > project root (./) > subdirectory, with more specific files overriding general ones.\n\nRemember: Claude Code = Anthropic's AI coding assistant CLI. Works in your terminal, understands your codebase, and helps write, debug, and refactor code.

column5: What are the three permission modes in Claude Code and when should you use each?
column6: Default mode asks before file edits and commands. Auto-accept edits mode allows file reads/writes but still asks for commands. YOLO mode auto-approves everything and should only be used for safe, isolated work — never on production infrastructure or shared systems.\n\nRemember: Claude Code asks permission before modifying files or running commands. Review changes before approving. Trust but verify.

column5: How do you create a custom slash command in Claude Code?
column6: Create a markdown file in .claude/commands/ directory. The filename (minus .md) becomes the command name. Use $ARGUMENTS as a placeholder for user input. Example: .claude/commands/deploy-check.md becomes /deploy-check. Team-shared commands go in the repo's .claude/commands/; personal commands go in ~/.claude/commands/.\n\nRemember: slash commands (/commit, /review-pr) invoke built-in skills. They're shortcuts for common workflows that Claude Code handles end-to-end.

column5: What are MCP servers in Claude Code and how are they configured?
column6: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers extend Claude Code with external integrations like databases, APIs, and internal tools. They are configured in .claude/settings.json under the mcpServers key, specifying a command, args, and environment variables. Use ${VAR} syntax for secrets — never hardcode credentials.\n\nRemember: Claude Code understands your project through CLAUDE.md files, directory structure, and code context. column5: What are Claude Code hooks and what events can they respond to?
column6: Hooks are shell commands that run automatically in response to Claude Code events. column5: How do you configure targeted tool permissions instead of using YOLO mode?
column6: Use claude config set allowedTools with an array of tool patterns. Examples: '["Bash(kubectl get *)", "Bash(kubectl describe *)"]' for read-only kubectl, '["Bash(make *)", "Edit", "Write"]' for build and edit permissions. This is safer than YOLO mode because it limits blast radius to approved operations.\n\nRemember: Claude Code asks permission before modifying files or running commands. column5: Why is YOLO mode dangerous for infrastructure work and what should you use instead?
column6: YOLO mode auto-approves all commands including terraform apply, kubectl delete, and rm -rf. One bad inference can destroy resources. Instead, use targeted permissions with allowedTools patterns that grant read-only access to production tools. Example: allow "kubectl get *" and "kubectl describe *" but not "kubectl delete *".\n\nRemember: Claude Code understands your project through CLAUDE.md files, directory structure, and code context. column5: What is the "overconfident commit" footgun and how do you prevent it?
column6: Claude Code can commit and push directly, including adding all files with git add -A (catching debug files, temp fixtures, IDE config). Prevent it by specifying target branches, requiring tests before commits, and adding git rules to CLAUDE.md: never push to main, always run make test, use feature branches.\n\nRemember: Claude Code understands your project through CLAUDE.md files, directory structure, and code context. column5: What happens when Claude Code's context window fills up during long sessions?
column6: Claude Code starts forgetting earlier conversation including your constraints and CLAUDE.md instructions. Signs: repeating failed approaches, losing track of modified files, ignoring instructions it followed earlier. Fix: use /compact at milestones, break long tasks into separate sessions, and watch the context usage indicator.\n\nGotcha: Claude Code has a context window limit. Keep prompts focused and provide relevant code snippets rather than entire files when possible.

column5: What makes an effective CLAUDE.md file?
column6: Include: stack and framework versions, validation/test commands (make test, ruff check), files that should not be modified (protected paths), naming conventions, commit message style, and a "Do NOT" section. Keep it concise — it's loaded every session and uses context window. Treat it like production config and keep it current.\n\nRemember: CLAUDE.md files provide repo-specific instructions. Precedence: direct user instruction > subtree CLAUDE.md > repo CLAUDE.md > workspace CLAUDE.md.

column5: How can MCP server configurations lead to credential leaks?
column6: MCP configs in .claude/settings.json may contain database passwords or API tokens. If hardcoded and committed to git, secrets end up in repo history. Fix: use environment variable references (${DATABASE_URL}) instead of literal values, and add .claude/settings.local.json to .gitignore for per-developer secrets.\n\nRemember: Claude Code understands your project through CLAUDE.md files, directory structure, and code context.
